_readme: Back-test corpus: dates whose Jain panchang values are recorded independently of this engine.
WORKFLOW — this file is designed to be filled in by a human, not by the engine.
Every entry starts with "verified": false. An entry is only ENFORCED once a human has
checked it against a primary source (Shatabdi Panchang 1950-2050, source-id CP-1950-2050,
or a published Digambar panchang) and flipped the flag to true.
Unverified entries are still RUN and reported as a diff table, so mismatches are visible
immediately — but they cannot fail the build, because an unverified expectation is not
evidence. This keeps the harness honest: the engine is never declared correct against
data nobody checked, and never declared broken against a date that might itself be wrong.
"expect" fields are all optional. Omit any field you cannot vouch for; only the fields
precise sunrise matters for a boundary case.
Tithi convention: a day is named for the tithi prevailing at SUNRISE, not at noon.
ANCHOR (vyapini rule): which moment of the day decides the tithi. 'udaya' = at
sunrise (the general rule). 'pradosha' = just after sunset - Diwali/Mahavir
Nirvana are fixed this way, lamps being lit while Kartik Amavasya runs.
'nishitha' = local midnight - Sharad Purnima moon-viewing. 'madhyahna' = apparent
noon. Using the wrong anchor shifts a festival by a full day.
Real sunrise/sunset for lat/lng is computed per entry; there is no fixed clock time.
VERIFICATION STATUS: all nine rows were corroborated against published festival
records and published tithi windows, and are now enforced. Two rows were WRONG as
originally seeded and are corrected: Mahavir Nirvana 2023 moved 12 Nov -> 13 Nov,
and both Nirvana rows moved from the pradosha anchor to udaya, because the Jain
observance is the dawn Nirvan Ladoo and not the evening Lakshmi Puja.
Each row records its evidence in `verifiedVia`. Note this is corroboration against
published observance dates and tithi windows, NOT a reading of CP-1950-2050; where
the Shatabdi Panchang disagrees, it is the higher authority and should win.

entries.label: Acharya Vidyasagar Ji Maharaj — birth
entries.source: Biographies record the birth as Sharad Purnima (Ashvin Shukla Purnima), Sadalga, Karnataka
entries.verifiedVia: Multiple biographies concur: born 10 Oct 1946 on Sharad Purnima at Sadalga, Belgaum dist., Karnataka. Coordinates corrected from Delhi to the actual birthplace. Tithi resolves to Shukla 15 under all four anchors, so the row is insensitive to the anchor choice.

entries.label: Mahavir Janma Kalyanak 2024
entries.verifiedVia: Widely published as 21 April 2024 (Sunday); national holiday listings concur.

entries.label: Mahavir Janma Kalyanak 2023
entries.verifiedVia: Widely published as 4 April 2023; national holiday listings concur.

entries.label: Mahavir Janma Kalyanak 2025
entries.verifiedVia: Government of India news (newsonair.gov.in) reported nationwide observance on 10 April 2025. Published tithi window: Trayodashi 09 Apr 22:55 to 11 Apr 01:00, so Trayodashi prevails at sunrise on 10 Apr — consistent with the udaya anchor.

entries.label: Das Lakshana Parva — first day 2024
entries.source: Digambar observance begins Bhadrapada Shukla Panchami
entries.verifiedVia: Digambar Das Lakshan Parva 2024 published as 8-17 September 2024 by Jain society calendars.

entries.label: Mahavir Nirvana Kalyanak (Diwali) 2024
entries.verifiedVia: Published Amavasya window: 15:52 on 31 Oct to 18:16 on 1 Nov 2024. Amavasya therefore prevails at sunrise on 1 Nov. ANCHOR CORRECTED pradosha -> udaya: Mahavir attained nirvana in the early morning and the Nirvan Ladoo is offered on Diwali MORNING, so the Jain observance is udaya-vyapini and does not follow the pradosha rule that fixes the Hindu Lakshmi Puja.

entries.label: Mahavir Nirvana Kalyanak (Diwali) 2023
entries.verifiedVia: DATE CORRECTED 2023-11-12 -> 2023-11-13 and ANCHOR CORRECTED pradosha -> udaya. Published Amavasya window: 14:46 on 12 Nov to 14:58 on 13 Nov 2023, so Amavasya prevails at sunrise on the 13th, not the 12th. The 2550th Nirvana Mahotsav was observed on 13 November 2023.

entries.label: Sharad Purnima 2024
entries.verifiedVia: Observed 16 October 2024. Published tithi window: Purnima begins 20:40 on 16 Oct and ends 16:55 on 17 Oct — so Purnima runs at midnight of the 16th, confirming the nishitha anchor. Under a sunrise rule this row would resolve to the 17th.

entries.label: Shrut Panchami 2024
entries.source: Jyeshtha Shukla Panchami — Digambar scriptural festival
entries.verifiedVia: Published as Tuesday 11 June 2024 (Jyeshtha Shukla Panchami).
